action.action-desc: Ms. Cortez Masto (for herself, Mr. Padilla, Mr. Van Hollen, Mr. Bennet, and Ms. Rosen) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance

form.official-title: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to extend and enhance certain tax credits for electric vehicles, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Cleaner Transportation Access for All Act.

section.header: Extension of credit for previously-owned clean vehicles

subsection.text: Section 25E(g) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by striking September 30, 2025 and inserting December 31, 2031.
The amendments made by this section shall apply to vehicles acquired after September 30, 2025.
Section 30D of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended—

paragraph.text: in subsection (e)—

subparagraph.text: in paragraph (1)(B)(iv), by striking during calendar year 2026 and inserting after December 31, 2025, and
in paragraph (2)(B)(iii), by striking during calendar year 2026 and inserting after December 31, 2025, and

paragraph.text: in subsection (h), by striking September 30, 2025 and inserting December 31, 2031.

subsection.text: The amendments made by this section shall apply to vehicles acquired after the date of enactment of this Act.

section.header: Extension and enhancement of alternative fuel vehicle refueling property credit

subsection.text: Section 30C(i) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by striking June 30, 2026 and inserting December 31, 2031.

paragraph.header: Elimination of eligible census tract requirement
paragraph.text: Section 30C(c) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by striking paragraph (3).

paragraph.header: Vehicle charging equipment installed at a residence
paragraph.text: Section 30C(c) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended by paragraph (1), is amended by adding at the end the following new paragraph:

paragraph.header: Vehicle charging equipment installed at a residence
paragraph.text: In the case of an individual, with respect to any qualified alternative fuel vehicle refueling property which is—

subparagraph.text: installed on or in connection with a dwelling unit which is used as a residence by such individual, and
capable of charging the battery of a motor vehicle propelled by electricity,

paragraph.continuation-text: subsection (a) shall be applied by substituting 50 percent for 30 percent.

subsection.text: The amendments made by this section shall apply to property placed in service after the date of enactment of this Act.

section.header: Exempt facility bonds for zero-emission vehicle infrastructure

subsection.text: Section 142 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended—

paragraph.text: in subsection (a)—

subparagraph.text: in paragraph (16), by striking or at the end;
in paragraph (17), by striking the period at the end and inserting , or; and
by adding at the end the following new paragraph:

paragraph.text: zero-emission vehicle infrastructure.
by adding at the end the following new subsection:
For purposes of subsection (a)(18), the term zero-emission vehicle infrastructure means any property (not including a building and its structural components) if such property is—

subparagraph.text: made available for use by—

clause.text: members of the general public,
residents of a multi-family residential building, or
employees of a workplace or customers at a commercial location, and

subparagraph.text: used to charge or fuel zero-emissions vehicles, but only if the property is located at the point where the vehicles are charged or fueled.

paragraph.text: The term zero-emission vehicle infrastructure shall include any utility service connections, utility panel upgrades, or contributions in aid of construction (as described in section 118) which are required for the charging or fueling of zero-emissions vehicles.

subparagraph.text: The term zero-emissions vehicle means—

clause.text: a zero-emission vehicle as defined in section 88.102–94 of title 40, Code of Federal Regulations (as in effect on the date of enactment of this subsection), or
a vehicle that, under any possible operational modes and conditions, produces zero exhaust emissions of—

subclause.text: any criteria pollutant for which there are national ambient air quality standards under section 109 of the Clean Air Act (42 U.S.C. 7409) or precursor pollutant, or

subparagraph.text: For purposes of this paragraph, the term greenhouse gas means any of the following:

clause.text: Carbon dioxide.
Methane.
Nitrous oxide.
Hydrofluorocarbons.
Perfluorocarbons.
Sulfur hexafluoride.

paragraph.header: Zero-emissions vehicle infrastructure located within other facilities or projects
paragraph.text: For purposes of subsection (a), any zero-emission vehicle infrastructure located within—

subparagraph.text: a facility or project described in subsection (a), or
an area adjacent to a facility or project described in subsection (a) that primarily serves vehicles traveling to or from such facility or project,

paragraph.continuation-text: shall be treated as described in the paragraph in which such facility or project is described.

subsection.text: The amendments made by this section shall apply to obligations issued after the date which is 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act.

section.header: Joint Office of Energy and Transportation

subsection.text: In addition to existing duties, the Joint Office of Energy and Transportation shall—

paragraph.text: support in the administration of grants under section 151(f) of title 23, United States Code, and the program described in section 8(a);

serve as the Federal coordinating body and source of information, technical assistance, and coordination with respect to the expansion of the use of electric vehicles, including by developing a publicly accessible website with essential information relating to electric vehicles, such as—

subparagraph.text: a map that depicts the nationwide network of electric vehicle charging infrastructure, including such publicly accessible infrastructure available at Federal facilities or sites, such as facilities and land owned or managed by the National Park Service and the Forest Service;
a complete listing of Federal incentives and funding opportunities related to electric vehicles and electric vehicle charging infrastructure; and
a catalog of incentives and funding opportunities offered by each State related to electric vehicles and electric vehicle charging infrastructure;

paragraph.text: coordinate with, and provide advice to, other Federal agencies, including the Environmental Protection Agency, the Department of Agriculture, the Department of Commerce, the Department of the Interior, the Department of the Treasury, the Department of Defense, the General Services Administration, the National Science Foundation, and any other relevant Federal agency, as determined by the Secretary of Energy and the Secretary of Transportation, with respect to the electrification of the United States transportation network through vehicles, charging infrastructure, and the supply chains of vehicles and charging infrastructure;

coordinate within the Department of Transportation to ensure minimum standards for electric vehicle charging infrastructure, with the goal of ensuring technological neutrality within in a manner that supports and reflects advancements in technology and changing fleet and consumer needs;
provide technical assistance and advice to the electric vehicle industry and electric vehicle users to support the increased use of electric vehicles, including—

subparagraph.text: State, Tribal, and local communities, including governmental agencies and departments in those communities responsible for public works and infrastructure, airport authorities, local school districts, and other entities as appropriate;
the domestic and imported automobile industry;
the medium- and heavy-duty truck industry, fleets, ports, and intermodal logistics facilities operators;
transit agencies and other public sector fleets;
electric utilities and other domestic energy providers, including the transportation fueling industry;
the workforce and organized labor in industries associated with transportation electrification, including entities that provide educational and workforce training and enhanced worker safety;
the battery supply chain, the critical minerals supply chain, and other supply chains for vehicles and charging infrastructure;
the travel, tourism, and outdoor recreation industries and the communities that support those industries, including high mileage fleets such as taxis and transportation network companies;

law enforcement and first responders, including by sharing information to support those entities in engaging with electric vehicle technology, including safety and fire issues, such as new tools and practices to combat and safely control electric vehicle battery fires; and
any other sectors, as the Secretary of Energy and the Secretary of Transportation determine to be appropriate; and

paragraph.text: consider increased adoption of electric vehicles at locations that support tourism, including around airports, and consideration of ways to support travel, tourism, and outdoor recreation sectors, including through taking actions described in section 8(d).

subsection.text: The table of contents in section 1(b) of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (Public Law 117–58; 135 Stat. 434) is amended by striking the item relating to section 25006 and inserting the following:

There is authorized to be appropriated $5,000,000,000 for the period of fiscal years 2027 through 2031, to remain available until expended, for the National Electric Vehicle Formula Program described in paragraph (2) of the matter under the heading highway infrastructure program under the heading Federal Highway Administration under the heading Department of Transportation in title VIII of division J of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (Public Law 117–58; 135 Stat. 1421) (commonly known as the National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Formula Program) (referred to in this section as the program), of which—

paragraph.text: $3,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2031 shall be used to carry out section 25006 of that Act (23 U.S.C. 151 note; Public Law 117–58); and
$150,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2031 shall be for administration of the Joint Office of Energy and Transportation.
For the period of fiscal years 2027 through 2031, as part of the plan submitted by each State in carrying out the program, each State shall include the strategy of the State—

subparagraph.text: to have completed any applicable infrastructure investments for the alternative fueling corridors in the State, which may include publicly available charging infrastructure not funded under the program or otherwise operated by a private entity;

to review and report existing charging infrastructure to best understand any needed maintenance, repairs, or upgrades to ensure the infrastructure is in working order and can support the traveling public;
to review and report on efforts to ensure signage, mapping, and consumer education to ensure the awareness of charging infrastructure by road users;
after completing investments under subparagraph (A)—

clause.text: to use not less than 20 percent of the amounts allocated to the State during the period to address the remaining needs of the underserved in urban and other non-rural communities;
to use not less than 20 percent of the amounts allocated to the State during the period to address the remaining needs of underserved rural communities;

to use not less than 20 percent of the amounts allocated to the State during the period for planning and support for the development and deployment of charging infrastructure for medium and heavy-duty electric vehicles; and

to use not more than 10 percent of the amounts allocated to the State during the period for issues relating to workforce and safety of electric vehicles, such as workforce training, recruitment, planning with local governments, and safety planning and preparations with law enforcement and first responders; and

subparagraph.text: in carrying out subparagraph (D), to create opportunities for individual communities, nonprofits, or private sector applicants to apply for individual subgrants to address public-facing charging needs for the residents, customers, or workers of those entities.

paragraph.text: The Secretary of Transportation, in consultation with the Joint Office of Energy and Transportation, may waive 1 or more requirements under paragraph (1) with respect to 1 or more States if the Joint Office determines that there would be significant challenges or if a requirement would not be feasible.

paragraph.header: Use of funds for grid upgrades
paragraph.text: In carrying out the program, a State may use not more than 20 percent of the amounts apportioned to the State for energy grid upgrades to support electric vehicle charging infrastructure.

In carrying out the program, the Secretary of Transportation shall review, and update as appropriate, regulations to carry out the program to include updated standards, including standards to support charging for medium- and heavy-duty vehicles and that recognize the distinct business case of fleet charging.

Not later than June 1 of each year, the Joint Office of Energy and Transportation shall submit to the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate, the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate, and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives a report on the implementation of the program, including, for the applicable period—

subparagraph.text: a description of the status of the plan of each State submitted in carrying out the program and whether the plan has been approved;
a description of the funds provided to each State under the program;
an identification of, for each State, charging infrastructure installed or repaired using funds under the program; and
the extent to which States have complied with subsections (b) and (d) and the status of implementation of those subsections.

paragraph.text: Not later than 30 days after the date on which a report is submitted under paragraph (1), the Joint Office of Energy and Transportation shall make the report publicly available on the website of the Joint Office.

subsection.header: Increased adoption of electric vehicles at locations that support tourism, including around airports

paragraph.text: The Joint Office of Energy and Transportation and the Federal Highway Administration shall, in carrying out the program, include consideration of increased adoption of electric vehicles at locations that support travel, tourism, and outdoor recreation sectors, including around airports, including by—

subparagraph.text: requiring States and other recipients of funding under the program to provide planning for charging infrastructure that supports—

clause.text: popular corridors for long-haul travel;
popular destinations and attractions for tourists;

electrification strategies for increased adoption of electric vehicles and charging infrastructure at and around medium hub airports and large hub airports (as those terms are defined in section 47102 of title 49, United States Code);
the travel and tourism sectors, including rental cars, taxis, rideshares, and other similar shuttle services to expand the adoption of electric vehicles;

the outdoor recreation industry through the use of electric vehicles and charging infrastructure, including at and around Federal sites and land managed by a Federal agency, including the National Park Service, the Forest Service, and other Federal land management agencies; and
locations not more than 25 miles from Federal sites and land described in clause (v); and

subparagraph.text: emphasizing the importance of driver education on where and how to charge an electric vehicle when traveling within the State or locality.

paragraph.text: In carrying out paragraph (1), the Joint Office of Energy and Transportation and the Federal Highway Administration shall consult with travel and tourism industry stakeholders, including the private sector, State tourism offices, and destination marketing organizations.

The Joint Office of Energy and Transportation and the Federal Highway Administration shall issue guidance to clarify that funding under the program may be used to support highway and Interstate access and units of the National Park System, national forests, and other land and sites managed by a Federal land management agency.

section.header: Strategies to reduce the cost of transportation fuels in the United States

subsection.text: In this section:

paragraph.text: The term Administrator means the Administrator of General Services.
The term Chair means the Chair of the Council on Environmental Quality.
The term Director means the Director of the Office of Management and Budget.

The term strategies means the short-term and long-term strategies to reduce the cost of transportation fuels for consumers in the United States through Federal conservation developed under subsection (b).
The term transportation fuel has the meaning given the term in section 211(o)(1) of the Clean Air Act (42 U.S.C. 7545(o)(1)).

Not later than 120 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Director, the Administrator, and the Chair, in coordination with the heads of other relevant Federal agencies, shall develop and publicly release short-term and long-term coordinated strategies to reduce the cost of transportation fuels for consumers in the United States through Federal conservation.
The strategies shall include—

subparagraph.text: a plan on how the General Services Administration can immediately reduce fuel consumption by the Federal Government in the period during which the increase in the cost of transportation fuel per gallon in the United States as compared to the previous year is 33 percent or more;

a plan to reduce the usage of transportation fuels by vehicles in the Federal fleet by 10 percent below the average amount of transportation fuels used by those vehicles year over year, subject to the condition that the plan shall not apply to transportation fuels needed for national defense, homeland security, or law enforcement purposes of the United States;

an assessment of and report on the availability of alternative transportation fueling options, such as electrification, through Federal fleets and personal vehicles used by Federal employees, for each Federal agency; and
recommendations to Congress on any legislation, authorities, or administrative actions necessary to reduce the cost of transportation fuels for consumers in the United States.

subsection.text: The Director, the Administrator, and the Chair, in coordination with the heads of other relevant Federal agencies, shall implement the strategies developed under subsection (b) as quickly as practicable after those individuals determine that the increase in the cost of transportation fuel per gallon in the United States as compared to the previous year is 33 percent or more.

The Director, the Administrator, and the Chair, in coordination with the heads of other relevant Federal agencies, shall cease implementing the strategies developed under subsection (b) on the date on which the increase in the cost of transportation fuel per gallon in the United States as compared to the previous year is less than 33 percent for a consecutive period of 180 days beginning after the implementation of those strategies.

In measuring the increase in the cost of transportation fuel per gallon in the United States under this section, the Director, the Administrator, and the Chair, in coordination with the heads of other relevant Federal agencies, shall use data from the Motor Gasoline Price Survey of the Energy Information Administration.
The strategies developed under subsection (b) shall not apply to—

paragraph.text: vehicles in the Federal fleet that are not under the management of the Administrator; or
vehicles under the management of the United States Postal Service.
